title: The degraded drill expected an empty page read to land; HW3 made it fail
body:
## Summary
tools/engine-degraded-fixtures.json:19 asserted that a read with no items lands (200); since 7e7a0740 (HW3) the read route fails it with the desk sentence, so the drill was red and unwired from CI.

## Description
desk/src/app/api/read/route.ts:45 throws DeskSaid(EMPTY_READ) for a read with no item, so Try again reads the page in place (desk/src/lib/desk/job.ts:67); tools/desk-jobs-rules-test.cjs:573-580 already pins it. The drill, harvested on 2026-10-20, still expected the old 200 and failed, which is why .github/workflows/harness-drills.yml:37-39 unwired its job. Fixed: the row expects the EMPTY_READ sentence and the drill's fails branch proves the page stays on the desk empty and a retry reads it.

## Flow
- vision stub answers {"items":[]} -> POST /api/read -> 502 EMPTY_READ
- fixture row expected lands:0 -> assertion 502 !== 200 -> drill exit 1
- fix: expect.fails = EMPTY_READ

## Expected impact
The drill is green again, so it can be wired back into CI (separate card). Nothing in the desk changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the drill asserts the read route's real fallback
Before: engine-degraded-test exit 1, 24 pass / 1 fail / 4 todo
After: exit 0, 25 pass / 0 fail / 4 todo (re-measured on the commit)
Method: gate - the drill itself, red then green
Result: better
Gate: none

title: A todo row that passes cannot fail: the clamp row in the drill now binds
evidence:

desk/src/lib/desk/read.ts:104-106 unit() and at() clamp (d86b7162, 2026-10-09)
before: "✔ read: centres outside the photo # read.ts trusts..." (a passing todo)
seed (unit/at unclamped) after the fix: exit 1, "✖ read: centres outside the photo"
body:
## Summary
The drill row for centres outside the photo kept a todo after d86b7162 clamped every centre and band into the page, so it passed as a todo and a regression of that clamp could never fail the suite.

## Description
node:test reports a todo test's failure without failing the run. desk/src/lib/desk/read.ts:104-106 clamps positions since d86b7162, and the row passed (reported as a passing todo) - the gap it named is closed, but the todo kept the row non-binding. Fixed by removing the todo; the three todo rows left all fail today and name real gaps (read.ts blank item, hint.ts blank hint x2).

## Flow
- seed: unit() and at() in read.ts made identity -> with todo: a todo failure, exit 0 (as the 3 failing todo rows exit 0 today)
- without todo: exit 1, "read: centres outside the photo" failed
- seed reverted byte for byte -> exit 0

## Expected impact
A regression that lets a model centre run off the page (an inverted crop band on the TV) now fails the drill. Nothing in the desk changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a fixed gap stays fixed
Before: 4 todo rows, 1 passing; the seeded clamp regression is not a failure
After: 3 todo rows, all failing real gaps; the seed -> exit 1; reverted -> exit 0, 26 pass / 0 fail / 3 todo
Method: gate - the drill with a seeded regression on both sides
Result: better
Gate: none

title: The degraded drill met 3 of 5 thrown failure kinds; it now reads them from EngineErrorKind
evidence:
tools/engine-degraded-test.cjs (old GUARD) for(const kind of ['timeout','unreachable','exit'])
desk/src/lib/engines/types.ts:62 type EngineErrorKind = "shape" | "timeout" | "exit" | "unreachable" | "cutoff" | "declined"
desk/src/lib/desk/job.ts:63-64 cutoff / declined sentences
desk/src/lib/desk/failure.ts:22 cutoff: false, declined: false (not retryable)
derived GUARD alone: exit 1 "no read row where the engine fails with cutoff"
new rows first run: 4 fail, "a retry reads the same page once the engine is back 409 !== 200"
body:
## Summary
The drill's GUARD typed its own list of failure kinds (timeout, unreachable, exit); types.ts gained cutoff and declined in 48ea6b82 and neither was driven through the read or hint route.

## Description
Two implementations of one list: desk/src/lib/engines/types.ts:62 (six kinds) and the GUARD's three. Each newer kind has its own desk sentence (desk/src/lib/desk/job.ts:63-64) and retry rule (desk/src/lib/desk/failure.ts:22: not retryable), unexercised at the screen. The GUARD now reads the union from types.ts (comments stripped, shape excluded) and asks for every kind on both read and hint; four rows were added. Building them showed the drill's own assumption was wrong for these kinds: every fails row asserted Try again works, while a ceiling or refusal is refused (409 NOT_AGAIN) by design. Rows with again:false now assert that refusal and that no second run starts.

## Flow
- derive kinds from types.ts -> GUARD red (no cutoff row)
- add cutoff and declined rows for read and hint -> 4 red: retry 409
- add again:false + refusedAgain() asserting 409, NOT_AGAIN, same job id -> green

## Expected impact
A new EngineErrorKind cannot ship without the drill showing what the TV says for it, and the no-retry rule for ceilings and refusals is now pinned at the route. Nothing in the desk changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every attempt-failure kind is driven through the TV routes
Before: 0 of 2 newer kinds driven; GUARD from a 3-entry hand list
After: 5 of 5 thrown kinds on each of read and hint; drill exit 0, 33 tests, 30 pass / 0 fail / 3 todo
Method: gate - derived GUARD red, then rows green
Result: better
Gate: none

title: A failed usage-ledger rotation dropped the row, and every row after it
evidence:
desk/src/lib/engines/meter.ts (before) try { ...; if (size > cap) { try { unlinkSync(old) } catch {}; renameSync(file, old); } appendFileSync(...) } catch (e) { log once per reason }
tools/econ-rules-test.cjs case g2: usage.1.jsonl a non-empty directory, cap 10 B, 3 calls -> 0 of 3 rows before, 3 of 3 after
body:
## Summary
desk/src/lib/engines/meter.ts ran the rotation inside the append's try, so a rename that fails (a held file on Windows) skipped the append and every later call hit the same failure - logged once, then silent.

## Description
cost-metering / usage-ledgers: "a best-effort ledger write whose failures are swallowed uncounted ... claims a completeness it no longer has". Past the cap, each call unlinks usage.1.jsonl and renames usage.jsonl over it; a rename failure threw to the outer catch before appendFileSync, and the once-per-reason log meant the second and later drops said nothing. Fixed: the rotation has its own try, its failure is said once ("could not be rotated"), and the row is appended so the file grows past its cap rather than going quiet.

## Flow
- ledger past DESK_USAGE_MAX_BYTES and usage.1.jsonl not replaceable
- call -> meter() -> renameSync throws -> append skipped -> one console.error
- every following call: same throw, no append, no log
- fix: rotation failure isolated; append always runs

## Expected impact
The operator's spend and outcome rows keep landing while a reader holds the file; the file may exceed 5 MB until the hold ends. Risk: none for the call (meter never throws).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - no ledger row is lost to a failed rotation
Before: econ case g2: 0 of 3 rows booked (exit 1)
After: 3 of 3 rows booked, the failure said once; econ-rules-test exit 0 (21 pass); engines, error-doors, prompt-assembly suites, tsc and desk-boundaries exit 0
Method: gate - a new econ case red then green
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Piper's input error was swallowed, and the silent-catch ratchet could not see it
evidence:
desk/src/lib/engines/voice.ts:58 (before) p.stdin.on("error", () => {});
desk/src/lib/engines/text.ts:95 and desk/src/lib/engines/codex.ts:61 reject the same event as EngineError("exit", "... closed its input")
tools/error-doors-test.cjs silentCatches(): matched catch {} and .catch(() => {}) only
extended ratchet: "src/lib/engines/voice.ts: 1 silent (allowed 0) at lines 58" exit 1; grep of the pattern over desk/src: 1 hit
body:
## Summary
desk/src/lib/engines/voice.ts:58 swallowed piper's stdin error with an empty listener, while text.ts and codex.ts reject the same event; the zero-site silent-catch ratchet in tools/error-doors-test.cjs did not count that shape.

## Description
A pair across three spawned engines: two route the stdin error to EngineError("exit"), one swallows it, so a piper that stopped reading part way could return a WAV of part of the line as a successful speak. The ratchet (burned to zero 2026-10-15) only matches catch blocks; it now also counts an .on/.once('error', () => {}) listener that does nothing, matched before its string-blanking step (which erases the event name), with four canary lines. voice.ts rejects like its siblings. (Commit body cites codex.ts:59; the line is codex.ts:61.)

## Flow
- extend silentCatches with the error-listener pattern + canaries -> red on voice.ts:58
- voice.ts: reject(new EngineError("exit", reported, "piper closed its input: ..."))
- error-doors green, SILENT stays {}

## Expected impact
A part-spoken line is reported as a failed speak, so the TV falls back to the browser voice; any future empty error listener in desk/src fails the gate.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a failure in the speak path leaves a trace
Before: ratchet blind to the shape; 1 silent error listener in desk/src
After: 0; error-doors-test exit 0 (10 pass), engines, econ, voice-rules suites and tsc exit 0
Method: gate - extended ratchet red then green
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Owner decision: the usage ledger loads lib/dataDir.ts across the engine seam
evidence:
tools/desk-boundaries.cjs:51-53 OWED engines-leaf meter.ts -> desk/src/lib/dataDir.ts, "whether a leaf helper may sit under the engine seam is open"
desk/src/lib/engines/meter.ts:28 usageFile() -> dataDir()
desk/src/lib/dataDir.ts:1-7 imports only node:path
meter() callers: desk/src/lib/engines/call.ts:194,199 only
body:
## Summary
The one owed layering break: desk/src/lib/engines/meter.ts loads desk/src/lib/dataDir.ts (a 7-line helper importing only node:path); closing it needs a rule choice the OWED entry already names as the owner's.

## Description
Three ways out, each measured against the tree: (a) the meter takes its directory from its caller - its only caller is call.ts, which has no data directory either, so the value would thread through every engine request or a module-level setter the session must call before any engine runs (an ordering hazard for the rules suites); (b) inline DESK_DATA_DIR || cwd/data in meter.ts - reopens the two-implementations pair de7361f2 closed ("the data directory is derived by one helper"), so it needs a parity test; (c) let desk-boundaries.cjs admit a leaf helper (a module whose own imports are only Node built-ins) under engines-leaf - a loosening of a layering check, which this round may not decide. None is S/M risk<=3 without a policy call.

## Flow
- owner picks (a), (b) or (c)
- (c): one rule in tools/desk-boundaries.cjs plus a suite case, OWED entry deleted
- (b): inline + an engines case holding usageFile() to path.join(dataDir(), "usage.jsonl") under three env states

## Expected impact
desk-boundaries prints 0 owed. Under (c) a future engine may load any built-in-only helper.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the engine seam holds without an owed entry
Before: 1 owed break
After: 0 under any option; the figure is the same, the rule is the decision
Method: simulation - the three options walked against call.ts, de7361f2 and the checker; nothing can measure which rule is right
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: architecture

title: A timeout the call core ends is booked under the provider name without its model
instrument: an econ case: a claude-cli-shaped stub that reports claude-cli/haiku on success and never settles on a second call; assert both rows share the provider string
evidence:
desk/src/lib/engines/call.ts:183 new EngineError("timeout", p.name, ...)
desk/src/lib/engines/call.ts:199 provider: err.provider || p.name
desk/src/lib/engines/text.ts:61 reported = claude-cli/${MODELS[...]}
docs/economics/ec1-sample-2026-10-10.jsonl: 13 rows all "claude-cli/haiku"
body:
## Summary
Success and provider-thrown rows say claude-cli/haiku; a timeout the call core declares (desk/src/lib/engines/call.ts:183) says claude-cli, so timeouts sit in a different provider bucket from the calls they belong to.

## Description
usage-ledgers: "the concrete model identifier as served". The core races the provider and rejects with p.name before the provider can report; the CLI's own abort-path error (text.ts:91) loses the race. Fix: Provider gains an optional reports(req) the core uses for its own timeout row (text: claude-cli/<model>, codex: codex/<model>, ollama: ollama/<model>). Touches types.ts, call.ts and four providers: M.

## Flow
- a claude call runs past its deadline
- call.ts rejects EngineError("timeout", "claude-cli") -> meter row provider "claude-cli"
- a "timeouts per model" query over the ledger finds none for claude-cli/haiku

## Expected impact
Timeout rate per model becomes readable from the ledger. Risk: a provider string change on timeout rows only.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every row of one model carries one provider string
Before: core-timeout rows: provider without model (1 of 6 outcome kinds)
After: 0 of 6 (predicted)
Method: simulation - walked call.ts:183/199 against text.ts:61; econ case b shows the core-timeout row naming the stub's bare name
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Dropped usage-ledger writes are logged once and never counted
instrument: econ case f extended: after N failed writes, a counter read through the engine status (/api/smoke) equals N
evidence:
desk/src/lib/engines/meter.ts say(): logged Set, one console.error per distinct reason
tools/econ-rules-test.cjs:134-139 case f: two failed writes -> one console.error, no count anywhere
cost-metering usage-ledgers smell: "a best-effort ledger write whose failures are swallowed uncounted"
body:
## Summary
meter.ts logs a failed ledger write once per reason and keeps no count, so the ledger cannot say how many calls it is missing.

## Description
cost-metering: "Choose per spend class, say which you chose, and count every dropped write." The desk chose best-effort (a write never throws into a call), which is right; the count is what is missing. Fix: a module counter of dropped rows (and of failed rotations) exposed beside the engine status rows in desk/src/lib/engines/health.ts, so the TV's engine check says "the ledger has missed N calls". Touches meter.ts, health.ts and the smoke route's suite: M.

## Flow
- ledger path unwritable
- every call: row dropped, first one logged
- operator reads the ledger as complete

## Expected impact
The operator can tell a quiet evening from a ledger that stopped writing.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the ledger states its own completeness
Before: 0 counters; case f: 2 drops, 1 log line
After: a count of 2 readable from the engine check (predicted)
Method: simulation - walked case f; the counter surface is a design choice in health.ts
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Ledger retention is a size accident: rotation deletes history past ~10 MB
evidence:
desk/src/lib/engines/meter.ts:7-8 "past DESK_USAGE_MAX_BYTES (5 MB) it is renamed to usage.1.jsonl, replacing the older copy"
desk/src/lib/engines/meter.ts rotation: unlinkSync(old) then renameSync
usage-ledgers: "Retention is a policy, not an accident ... rows are financial evidence, retained on declared terms"
body:
## Summary
The usage ledger keeps at most two 5 MB files; each rotation deletes the older one, so how far back spend and outcome history goes depends on call volume, not on a declared term.

## Description
cost-metering / usage-ledgers: retention is declared, never inherited from a size cap. At the EC1 sample's ~330 bytes a row, 10 MB is ~30k calls. Today every price is 0 or null and no budget sums the ledger, so nothing is mis-enforced yet; but drift and economics reviews read it. Options: dated rotation (usage-YYYY-MM.jsonl) with a declared prune horizon, or keep the cap and say the term. Deleting or keeping evidence is the operator's call.

## Flow
- ledger reaches 5 MB -> usage.1.jsonl replaced
- the older 5 MB of rows is gone with no record of the deletion

## Expected impact
An economics or drift question about last month may find the rows gone. Keeping more stores more on disk.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - retention is declared
Before: retention = 2 x 5 MB, size-driven
After: a declared term (owner decision)
Method: simulation - row size from docs/economics/ec1-sample-2026-10-10.jsonl; the term itself is a policy
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: irreversible
